prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which designed small molecules, from bifunctional PROTACs to cereblon-dependent molecular glues, direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to selected proteins

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation remains my first choice on the chemistry. A designed small molecule brings an E3 ligase and a chosen protein together, and the mechanism can be described in physical terms: ternary-complex cooperativity, linker geometry, degron recognition and the kinetics of ubiquitin transfer. This is a new modality that turns occupancy-driven pharmacology into event-driven removal of the target, and independent groups have confirmed it over two decades. My change this round is the third name. In round 1 I preferred Ciulli on the argument that his VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made PROTACs a general platform. The chair asked what single criterion should decide between Ciulli and Handa. My criterion is which strand carries the discovery that the citation must stand on, and which best answers the maturity objection that I myself raised. Handa's identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide explains a whole class of molecular glues, and the approved drugs lenalidomide and pomalidomide show that the mechanism has already been validated in patients. That is something the PROTAC strand cannot yet claim. Crews and Deshaies carry the concept of designed induced proximity, and Handa carries the mechanistic discovery behind the clinically proven half. A single citation can honestly cover both because both recruit a ligase to a protein that the cell would not otherwise degrade; I do not support a two-part prize, which would be artificial.
statement.case_against: No bifunctional degrader is approved, so the payoff of the PROTAC half is still forward-looking and a prize could be called early. The three-name limit also omits Ciulli, whose structure-guided work I still regard as the best physical chemistry in the field, as well as Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim. Whoever is omitted, part of the field will see the allocation as arbitrary, and I have moved off Ciulli with that cost in view. There is a real scientific argument that PROTACs and glues are two discoveries with different histories, and that a combined citation joins them more tidily than the history allows. If the committee cannot accept this configuration, Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B002) is the mature and cleanly attributed fallback.

responses.point: Andrei argues that Handa should rank ahead of Ciulli because cereblon is a target and mechanism discovery, and that thalidomide, lenalidomide and pomalidomide, which are approved, make glues the part of the field with proven clinical benefit.
responses.response: I have changed my position because of this argument. In round 1 I called cereblon a target-identification result in one drug class. The clinical point answers my own timing worry better than anything I said: if the committee is concerned about a prize before approval, the cereblon strand is already validated in patients and the citation can rest on it together with the PROTAC concept. I still think Ciulli's work is the best chemistry in the field and I regard his omission as a real cost, which I would not hide. But with only three places, the discovery of mechanism with proven medical consequences outweighs platform refinement. I agree with Andrei that the citation should be worded around the mechanism and not around one lineage.

responses.point: Daniel would accept Ciulli, but only with a citation narrowed to PROTACs, and says that Ciulli's work builds on the Crews and Deshaies concept while Handa's is the more clearly independent discovery.
responses.response: Daniel's point that Ciulli's contribution builds on an existing concept while cereblon is independent is the point I could not answer in round 1, and it is why I now accept Handa. It also settles the chair's question about narrowing: a PROTAC-only citation with Ciulli would leave the clinically proven strand uncredited, and I would rather keep the wider wording that names both. Where I would remain cautious is that the citation must not imply that Handa worked on PROTACs; the wording I propose describes the shared principle of directing the ubiquitin-proteasome system and names the two routes, bifunctional and glue.

responses.point: Peter argues that B002 should win because its attribution is already resolved, and that if the committee goes to B023 my structural argument favours Ciulli.
responses.response: I accept that B002 has the cleaner attribution and I have kept it as my first alternative. I do not agree that an unresolved third name should decide the discovery. Every member has acknowledged that the cut leaves out someone strong, but that is also true of many past prizes and does not make the science less sound. Peter is right that my structural argument pointed to Ciulli, and I have given that up for the reason that I gave Andrei, not because the argument is weak. On the 2010 point I agree with him that C-N coupling needed different ligand design and a different mechanistic solution at amine binding and reductive elimination, so I do not treat it as a repeat. I weigh it as a modest cost, and I still judge that a new modality is the stronger use of the prize this year.

responses.point: Xiaodong holds B002 first because discovery and credit are both settled, and says the PROTAC and cereblon lineages make the allocation in B023 harder than I admitted.
responses.response: The lineages are different and I do not claim otherwise. The reason I think one prize can still cover them is that Crews and Deshaies state the design principle and Handa supplies the mechanism that shows the same principle operating in approved drugs. That is a reasoned allocation and not a list of favourites. I agree with her that the timing concern is real; I now answer it with the thalidomide-class drugs and not with the ternary-complex chemistry alone. If she still sees no three-name set she can accept, I would like to know whether she objects to the single-citation idea or to the choice of names, because my answer to those would differ.

responses.point: Peter moved to B023 and holds B028 as his first alternative, while discounting his own bias because his research is close to it.
responses.response: I thank Peter for saying so openly and I will do the same for my side. He did not give the single sentence for B028 that I asked for in round 1, and the chair repeated the question. Without it I still cannot see Nocera, Meyer, Mayer and Hammes-Schiffer as one achievement, so I keep B028 only as my second alternative. I agree with him, as I do now with the Handa argument, that the committee should decide the third name explicitly and not by default.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands as one achievement for citation purposes, or whether a reviewer will find the combined wording misleading given the omission of Sakamoto, Gray, Ito, Kim and Ciulli.
Whether recognising the field before any bifunctional degrader is approved is premature; I have not verified the current clinical status.
Whether my move from Ciulli to Handa is the right weighing of platform generalisation against mechanistic discovery. I regard it as close and would not object strongly to the reverse.
Whether the 2010 cross-coupling prize should weigh against B002, which is my fallback.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal. None of the shortlisted candidates is a collaborator, supervisor or Uppsala colleague, and my postdoc with Arieh Warshel concerned EVB simulation, and he is not on the shortlist. My computational field overlaps scientifically with the theory strand of B028 (Hammes-Schiffer), which is proximity and not a personal tie, and it is another reason I hold B028 only as an alternative. I have served on the committee with Peter Brzezinski since 2015, which is not a conflict. No disclosure has changed since round 1.
